idiom_name: typed AsyncScope helper over Promise.all + AbortSignal (Awaited<T> result typing)
implementation_notes: The runtime semantics are exactly JavaScript's, so the realization is a typed scope helper: withScope<T> owns one AbortController, passes its signal to a callback whose promise it awaits, and aborts in finally; heterogeneous children keep their distinct types through Promise.all tuple inference, which TypeScript 4.5's Awaited type powers. Types document but do not enforce the structure - a floating promise is perfectly type-correct - so no-floating-promises lint rules and disciplined use of the helper carry the guarantee.
pitfalls: The type system cannot force a promise to be joined - `void someAsync()` compiles and leaks the child.
Promise.all tuple inference needs `as const` (or an explicit tuple type) for heterogeneous results to stay distinct.
DOM AbortSignal and Node's AbortSignal typings differ across lib targets; a shared scope helper should depend on the structural type rather than a global.
